_comment: Texture roles of satk.style.texture: what a texture is used for decides which vanilla distribution it is
compared with. 'match' = regular expressions on the texture name (first role that matches wins, in this
order); 'vanilla' = how the vanilla sample of the role is picked from the index (own textures of models of
these families/classes whose name matches). A role with fewer than min_samples vanilla textures falls back
Verdict: 'out' when a metric is beyond its fence (counts in log space: log_metrics), or when max_edges or more metrics sit outside p10..p90 at once (a texture at the edge of everything).

interior.what: car interior seen through alpha-128 glass: dark, low saturation, photo-like (vanilla sample: IDE type car)

body.what: vehicle body textures and paint jobs (own TXD)

_comment: Look advice of style.texture and the asset.check texture section (satk.style.texture.look_advice), against the vanilla
sample of the texture's role: 'flat/CG-clean' when tex.tone_mid (fine tonal variation) is below the role's tone_mid_pct
percentile, or tex.flat_share (dead-flat 5x5 patches) is above its flat_share_pct percentile and at least flat_share_min;
'too sharp' when tex.crisp (edge contrast / fine variation) is above its crisp_pct percentile. At p5/p95 about 5-8 % of
the vanilla sample of each role gets advice (decals and car paint are flat by design: their own bands allow it). The bin of
the first atelier run (ls_bin_paint, role prop): tone_mid 0.81 (vanilla prop p5 1.3, p50 7.3), flat share 0.66 (p95 0.27),
crisp 72 (p95 43): both. Advice only: never a gate.
